subject: Startups
title: Dropbox's Referral Program
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dropbox's Referral Program.

hook.text: Dropbox spent $300 per customer on Google ads. The product cost $99 a year. The math didn't work.

buildup.text: Drew Houston tried a different approach: give users 500 MB of free storage for every friend they referred.

discovery.text: Referrals increased sign-ups by 60%. The cost per user dropped from $300 to virtually nothing.

twist.text: The program was two-sided: both the referrer and the friend got free space. Both had a reason to act.

climax.text: Dropbox went from 100K to 4 million users in 15 months, mostly through referrals. No traditional ads needed.

punchline.text: Pay with product, not with ad dollars.

quiz.question: How much did Dropbox's sign-ups increase from its referral program?
